name: Using the design system in Vue 2
summary: New UI in the legacy Vue 2 apps (presenter, audience, admin) uses the DS <aha-*> web components, never the old stpancras-storybook-app kit: load lib/all.js + tokens.css once pinned to a tag, set Vue.config.ignoredElements = [/^aha-/], bind arrays with .prop and read CustomEvent detail. Existing screens stay as they are unless a task asks to migrate them.
highlights: New UI in the legacy Vue 2 apps uses DS <aha-*> web components
Load lib/all.js and tokens.css once, pinned to a tag; existing screens stay as they are
lead: Vue 2 renders custom elements natively, so the same <aha-*> elements React and Vue 3 use work in the legacy apps with no adapter. This guide covers the four things that differ: loading, telling Vue the tags are custom elements, binding props, and listening to events — plus the scope rule for new versus existing screens.

skillRef.note: Consumer guide for Vue 2 apps. The aha-design plugin links here instead of restating it.

rules.rule: New UI in a Vue 2 app (new screen, panel, dialog or control) uses the DS <aha-*> elements — never a stpancras-storybook-app component.
Existing screens built on the kit stay as they are; migrate one to <aha-*> only when the task asks for it.
Load lib/all.js and tokens.css once for the whole app, pinned to a release tag — never @master and never per component.

Bind strings, numbers and booleans as attributes; bind arrays and objects as DOM properties with the .prop modifier; read event data from the CustomEvent's detail and ignore native events that bubble out of an input.
Size and style an <aha-*> only through its attributes and --aha-* tokens — never ::part sizing or recolouring.

reuseNote: Doc-only guide — the elements it uses are the ordinary DS exports in lib/all.js.
whenToRead: ANY new UI in a Vue 2 app (presenter, audience, admin, Nuxt 2): load <aha-*> via lib/all.js pinned to a tag, Vue.config.ignoredElements = [/^aha-/], .prop for arrays, $event.detail for events. New design uses <aha-*>, never stpancras-storybook-app; existing screens stay unless asked.
